text:
mike: Quick heads-up — after the kernel-selector tweak yesterday I'm seeing a ~7% drop in prefix cache hit-rate on the v2-kernel worker pool. Noticed a bunch of cold KV misses for the same customer prompts. :eyes:
anya: ugh. any spikes in latency or token cost delta?
pranav: profile attached to the runtime dashboard shows higher tokenization divergence for system+toolcall combos. Kernel selector now prefers short-seq kernels which do a slightly different tokenizer path for tool fields.
sophie: do you have a log sample? can we reproduce a cache-key mismatch locally?
mike: pasted a couple of sample entries from kvcache debug (redacted):
```
cache_key: sha256:4f8b2a...
prompt_signature: "usr:how_to_connect"
tokenizer_version: "tok_v202309"
system_prompt_hash: sha1:...
tool_fields: [{name: "getUser" , order: ["id","opts"]}]
```
and later a miss that should have hit with same prompt but token_version: "tok_v202311"
anya: so tokenizer_version drift + tool field ordering = different canonical key. That explains a cluster of misses. :bug:
lee: why did tokenizer_version change across kernels? I thought we pinned in the serving image.
pranav: the selector change re-routed short seqs to an optimized kernel image that built a newer tokenizer at build-time (minor bump). We assumed canonicalization would normalize token streams; apparently it doesn't for tool metadata serialization.
sophie: immediate mitigation: normalize tool/function param ordering and strip stable whitespace before hashing. I'll open a tiny patch that canonicalizes tool fields (sort keys + stable JSON stringify). That should collapse most differences.
mike: thanks — can we canary that? 5% traffic on dedicated first. Also propose runtime route metadata include explicit tokenizer_pin to prevent cross-kernel token changes for hot routes.
lee: we can add a route-level header: `X-Token-Pin: tok_v202309` and runtime will supply same tokenizer binary for that route. Will require a small config change in routing table.
pranav: longer term: kernel selector should include tokenizer-compat label so we don't mix incompatible tokenizers in same cache cohort. I'll add a label check to the selector (cheap).
anya: also check batching heuristics — if batcher mixes requests across kernel variants we could be forcing tokenization path switches mid-batch which might corrupt KV keys.
sophie: good call. I'll add a guard to batcher to avoid mixing routes without same tokenizer_pin/value.
mike: plan: (1) Sophie PR to canonicalize tool fields + whitespace (urgent), (2) Lee deploy route header support and canary X-Token-Pin on 5% (config only), (3) Pranav add tokenizer-compat label to selector and ban-mix in batcher, (4) monitor hit-rate and tail latency for 24h; rollback if hit-rate not back above baseline.
runtime-bot: deploy started: canary (eng-runtime-dedicated) 5% -> 2367012380
anya: I'll set up a quick eval that computes prefix hit-rate delta per cohort and alerts at -2.5% from baseline.
pranav: also posting a small profiler snippet — on miss traces the kernel-time is actually lower but the tokenization stage shows an extra 1-2ms for re-tokenizing tool fields. That's consistent with duplicate tokenizers.
mike: sounds good. Sophie/Lee — please attach PR links and estimated time to canary. I'll own monitoring + rollback criteria.
sophie: PR: https://git.redwood/s/sophie/toolfield-canonicalize (5 files, tiny). ETA 2h for review + canary.
lee: route header change PR in router repo: https://git.redwood/s/lee/route-tokenpin. ETA 3h to config + canary.
mike: thanks. if we see persistent regression after those, we revert kernel-selector change and force single kernel cohort until we finish a compatibility plan.
pranav: noted. I'll also run a small synthetic workload to estimate recovery on canary before routing more traffic.
anya: I'll drop raw hit-rate graphs to the thread when available. :thumbsup:
mike: perfect, appreciate the quick turnaround.
